question.text: Under Section 9.3 of the workbook (Penalties as per SEBI Act 1992), SEBI is empowered to initiate adjudication proceedings against intermediaries for defaults such as:

answer.text: Only failure to deposit the prescribed registration fee on time.
Only failure to appoint a Compliance Officer.
Only failure to adopt an anti-money-laundering policy.
Failure to furnish information / return / report, or failure to enter into an agreement with clients, among other specified defaults.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook and the SEBI Act 1992, SEBI may impose penalties and initiate adjudication against intermediaries on grounds such as failure to furnish information/return/report, failure to enter into an agreement with clients, and other specified defaults. The list is broader than fee-default, CO-appointment or AML alone. The Trap: Each of the narrow options captures only one slice of the actual grounds - the SEBI Act penalty regime addresses a much wider set including information, agreement, conduct and compliance failures. Cross-Exam Context: III-A/III-C and XXIV AML both test SEBI Act Sections 15A-15HB adjudication; XXIII imports the same framework to intermediaries that include SIAOs. Assessor's Pro-Tip: During onboarding of a new client engagement, confirm the SIAO has filed all SEBI returns due to date and has a written client agreement in place. Absence of either is a direct SEBI Act exposure that will also taint the SIA's assurance statement.
